title: Released TESS dip models show less depth-related widening than tested saturated Gaussian screens
abstract: We test whether changes in selected complex periodic variable dips follow scalar density changes in a fixed saturated Gaussian screen. We use released TESS harmonic models, local depth and width estimates, and matched screen controls. The strict selection gives six usable stars with a median log-width versus log-depth slope of 0.024 (95% star bootstrap interval -0.237 to 0.307). A second, post hoc selection gives 68 usable tracks in 42 stars and a slope of 0.034 (-0.069 to 0.176). On common tracks in 41 stars, the median real-minus-control slope is -0.235 for maximum core optical depth 3. Saturated controls widen more across three local baseline widths. A fixed-shape control is close to the data at the main baseline width. We provide a screen width law, a proof of the normalized wing response, numerical checks, code and aggregate evidence. This limits the tested smooth-screen density model. It does not set a general optical-depth bound: opaque coverage changes and other column shapes remain possible. The larger selection is post hoc, and controls act on harmonic coefficients rather than raw flux.

display.caption: Selected TESS dip models show less depth-related widening than tested saturated Gaussian screens. Dark points use baseline half-width 0.12 phase. Pale points use 0.10 and 0.14. Intervals resample stars. The larger sample is a post hoc selection.
